policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The number of required pick-ups comes from the goal instruction: 'pick up ... again' means 1 pick-up; 'for N times' (two, three, ...) means N pick-ups. An episode starts in subgoal A: pick up the cube, pointing at target_cube (the position of the cube that the demonstration picked up, derived from the demonstration steps at the first decision step and tracked through the shuffle swaps). Rules, applied at every decision step after updating memory: - If the scene at this decision step shows the gripper raised with fingers partly closed (about 46% open, not 100%), the robot is holding the cube, regardless of the table list (the held cube is usually still listed at its old position): choose B: put it down. - Otherwise (fingers 100% open; the robot holds nothing even if a cube is listed as 'lifted off the table', which is a cube just released and settling): if picks_done is less than the required number of pick-ups, choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at target_cube as updated at this step (after a put-down this is the current position of the cube the execution steps showed released); if picks_done equals or exceeds the required number, choose C: press the button to finish. If a situation matches no rule (for example the gripper state is ambiguous or target_cube cannot be matched to any listed cube), prefer: holding something -> B; not holding and picks_done below the requirement -> A at the cube nearest target_cube; else -> C. Always point at target_cube as updated at this step.

fields.name: target_cube
fields.description: Position [y, x] of the cube the demonstration picked, at its current table position. At the first decision step (memory empty), read the DEMONSTRATION STEPS: find the frame where the gripper is lowest (height about 0.02) and the fingers first read about 46%; the picked cube is the cube listed nearest the gripper's own [y, x] there (the 'held in the gripper' line in the following frames confirms it; a cube merely vanishing from the list while the gripper hovers over it is occlusion, not a pick). Then carry the 'picked' label through the shuffle one swap at a time. A swap is a run of frames in which exactly two listed positions leave their resting spots and, when the list is still again, the same two spots are filled again: the two movers have EXCHANGED spots. If the picked cube was one of the two movers, it is now on the OTHER mover's starting spot, never back on its own. If it was not a mover, it stays put. Do not use mid-crossing frames to decide where it lands; they only tell you a swap is happening. Repeat for every swap to the last demonstration frame, however many swaps occur and whatever partners they involve: two consecutive swaps of the same pair return it to its original spot; a swap of a different pair moves it elsewhere or leaves it alone, so it can end two or more spots from where it started. Do not decide by which cube is 'back' on the original pick spot: once any swap has touched that spot, the cube resting there afterwards is a different cube. Write the position of the labelled spot as listed in the scene at the start of execution. At every later decision step: if the execution steps shown include a frame where the gripper is at about height 0.02 with fingers partly closed and the fingers then reopen to about 100% at that height (a put-down), the released cube is the listed cube in the scene at this decision step that lies nearest the gripper's own [y, x] at that reopen frame: write that listed position. If it is absent from the list for a frame or two while the gripper rises over it, that is occlusion, not a sign that another listed cube is it; never locate it from 'held in the gripper' or 'lifted off the table' coordinates, which drift in mid-air. Otherwise write the position of the listed cube within about 10 px of the carried value, or copy the carried value if none is listed. Ignore 'lifted off the table' lines. e.g. [85, 109]

fields.name: picks_done
fields.description: Count of completed grasps. Write 0 at the first decision step (memory empty). At any later step, write the carried value plus one if the execution steps shown include a frame with the gripper at about height 0.02 and fingers going from 100% to about 46% (or any 'is held in the gripper' line) AND the scene at this decision step shows the gripper raised (height about 0.14 or more) with fingers about 46% open (not 100%). Do not require the cube to be missing from the table list; it is usually still listed at its old position. Otherwise, and always when the fingers at the scene are 100% open (even if a cube is listed 'lifted off the table'), copy the carried value unchanged. e.g. 2
